Primary audited checklist coverage, a conservative evidence-verified lower bound: **4/984 = 0.41%**. Each atomic mandatory hosting outcome has one binary point. Only `verified` earns a point. This measures evidence-complete coverage of this versioned checklist. It does not measure engineering effort, elapsed time, implementation completion, or an intrinsic percentage of Coolify.

Implementation presence is separate: 46 implemented, 300 partial, 638 missing. Verified: 4. These totals cannot be added.

Original inventory: 68 requirement parents, 37 acceptance parents, and 58 matrix parents: 19 areas, 9 databases, 10 sources, 3 secret providers, 7 builders, 4 proxies, and 6 notification channels. Parent/gate rows receive no extra score.

Fully complete requirement parents: 0/68. Acceptance gates passed: 0/37. Matrix gates passed: 0/58.

## Method and scope

Each criterion is a mandatory hosting outcome. Matrix breadth is expanded under its owning requirement and scores once. Acceptance scenarios and all matrix parents are binary release gates with zero extra weight.
Criteria were reviewed against the complete original R01-R68 text and the surrounding compatibility-ledger obligations. Full source rows and clause-review records remain in JSON. Compound runtime outcomes require the whole declared result, not a count of files, functions, commits or passing assertions.
Implementation presence records missing, partial or implemented. Evidence state records missing, partial, implemented, verified, evidence_unavailable or failed. Only verified contributes 1. Every other state contributes 0. A fully complete R requires all child criteria and applicable acceptance/matrix gates to pass.
R44 database rows duplicate the specification engine table and are cross-linked. The specification product-area table duplicates the ledger area inventory. Neither creates additional parent rows or points. Architecture/version, engine lifecycle, Compose raw/differential behavior, notification safety and extended infrastructure obligations are retained even when they are prose outside tables.
The denominator is a reviewed decomposition, not a mechanically discovered feature count. Source/inventory/hash checks establish integrity; independent specification review must assess whether all clauses are represented without duplicate outcomes.

Broad R08 Git/branch/commit choices cross-link the corresponding R09 source children; R44 engine rows specialize shared engine obligations and duplicate source tables add no score. Generic strategy outcomes and their specialized matrix outcomes were linked instead of scored twice where identified.
Original requirement sentences remain review units. The code validator checks their exact text and nonempty criterion links, but cannot prove human-language completeness or semantic nonduplication. Independent specification review is required before accepting this baseline.
Support-matrix criterion labels are proposed mandatory acceptance boundaries, not passing tests. A criterion containing a bounded compound outcome passes only when all named parts pass; one assertion never supplies fractional credit.

Scope exclusions and imported safety obligations:

- R69-R102 and A38-A66 are excluded from the primary hosting denominator. R07 imports the minimum R81/R82 untrusted-hosting isolation prerequisite. R13/R15 import the R87-R92 hosting input, trust, reuse and evidence-safety clauses. R17 imports R85 human production authorization for agent-produced work. These references do not make full workspace functionality a prerequisite for trusted hosting.
- R65 durable Task collaboration, goals/activity/workspace/checkpoint/checks/candidate/preview/budget/history UI is deferred. Direct navigation and hosting without a Task remain scored. R54 task-derived previews are conditional on a future Task implementation and are retained as an unverified declared hosting path.
- R68/A36 agreement of schema, API, permissions, audit, UI, operational behavior and tests is an aggregate release gate. It earns no extra feature point. Published support profiles and measured limits remain independently scored outcomes.
- Coolify client adapters are conditional release contracts. No endpoint/request/response/error/version inventory is declared, so their unresolved contract gate stays missing and outside the fixed hosting-feature denominator. No endpoint is invented and no empty inventory passes.
- Native Go agent instead of upstream SSH-only management is an explicit implementation difference. Test-CA HTTPS does not establish production DNS/ACME. Linux arm64 qualification does not establish amd64 or a full architecture/version matrix. Trusted Docker does not establish hostile-workload isolation.

Evidence certainty and known contradictions:

- The primary figure is a conservative evidence-verified lower bound at the pinned audit SHA. It is not the percentage of implementation completed: many bounded capabilities exist without retained, relevance-qualified acceptance for this exact outcome/profile. Missing evidence is not proof of missing code.
- No broad R, A or full matrix row has complete combined evidence at the audited SHA. Historical accepted foundations are real bounded accomplishments, but cannot be summed into a full journey or percentage.
- Database capture/replay and recovery: retained /tmp/nerocd-database-runner-20261024.askzxzjj/runtime-test passes at b7771468edf95f531c13d69b361ed901d9efbbc8. Engine/network/Go dependencies are unchanged, but coordinator/replay/journal/CLI/store changed by the audit. No current combined verified credit is retained.
- Uploaded-volume archive: /tmp/nerocd-storage-runtime-20261024.iWwXss/gate.log passes physical backup/new-volume restore with reads/writes and UID/GID/mode checks. Original source 2ba8041359576a32d616d7f83e0c7eafe4ee4d91, retained at 45298ea4bbd85c91ee4b0d4d64cd72d9346e1faa. Its 19 declared source blobs match, but shared runtime/journal/materialization dependencies changed. This is not transitive proof at the audit SHA and never proves database-native backup.
- Source/ledger discrepancy: RequestHostingDatabaseNetworkUpgrade is wired through store/River/coordinator apply/observe and an explicit CLI opt-in, with internal/api/hosting_database_upgrade_runtime_integration_test.go. Earlier ledger text says upgrade controller absent. Internal upgrade is implemented within its bounds; there is no public upgrade HTTP workflow or completed R42 application binding.
- Application binding: PutHostingDatabaseBinding persists internal prerequisites, explicitly neither schedules nor connects; the private applicationDatabaseEngine is unregistered and no public binding route exists. Do not infer a usable application/database journey from private helpers.
- Core runtime/browser retained logs have source-revision or transitive-dependency limitations. Readiness, SSH, push, route-switch and metadata-recovery historical passes are not silently promoted to current-SHA verified outcomes.
- Fresh harmless existing Go unit tests can verify only exact bounded invariants, with raw JSON pass output embedded in this checklist. They never qualify a UI-to-runtime journey. All other historical evidence is implementation/context evidence with limits.

A missing verification artifact or affected/unknown historical dependency removes verified credit. A source test is implementation evidence until its actual pass is retained. `partial` has zero points. No runtime tests are implied by generating this report.

The original source row is retained verbatim in JSON with its pinned SHA and line range. Criterion source links point to that full requirement. Read acceptance and matrix gates alongside the atomic checklist before making a release claim.

## Reproduce

Run from the repository root with Python 3 and Git. No network or third-party packages are required.

```sh
python3 -B scripts/parity_audit.py --write
python3 -B scripts/parity_audit.py --check
python3 -B scripts/parity_audit.py --self-test
```

`--check` validates the original inventory at the audited SHA, frozen criterion manifest, links, source ranges, evidence subjects and embedded pass artifacts, then rejects a stale generated report. `--self-test` exercises rejected missing/duplicate scope, invalid evidence and stale-report cases. Fresh harmless unit-check JSON output is preserved in the checklist. Historical `/tmp` runtime artifacts receive no current verified credit. This audit does not run application/runtime tests.

## Conditional client compatibility gate

Unresolved conditional Coolify client contract: select exact endpoints, versions, request/response/error behavior, authorization and lifecycle outcomes before implementing or claiming an adapter. No endpoint inventory is declared. Contract selection and its tests remain a required gate for any future client-compatibility claim; zero selected endpoints is not a pass.

Schema 1; scoring `hosting-atomic-v1`. Criterion IDs and outcome definitions are frozen for this baseline. A future scope revision must record added and removed IDs and publish both the old and new denominator. Changing evidence does not change the denominator.

## Update the audit

1. For evidence-only refresh, choose an exact clean candidate and update audit_sha plus scripts/parity_audit.py BASE together. Re-extract original source ranges/text at that candidate and compare changes. Preserve criterion IDs, outcome definitions and denominator. Update source-manifest hash constants if source ranges move, while preserving outcome definitions; any semantic scope change follows the separate scoring-version procedure.
2. Recheck each credited test subject and complete relevant source/test/config/tool/dependency inputs. Retain unchanged historical credit only with explicit relevance; affected or unknown evidence becomes unverified until rerun. Update embedded pass artifacts, exact tests, profile and limits.
3. For a true scope change, increment scoring_version and schema/history handling, record every added/removed criterion ID with reason, and publish old/new denominator. Update the calculator frozen inventory/manifest rules through review. Never silently reweight outcomes.
4. Regenerate the report with --write, run --check and --self-test, review specification and code hygiene at the same candidate, and commit the audit. No latest-main inference or automatic credit from passing-test counts is allowed.
